title: 140,752 alphabets that are not keyword alphabets (first-appearance orders from the sculpture's texts, QWERTY, Morse and frequency orders): key-rule battery, sentence-key score, and two-alphabet join for key lengths 1-20
k4_result: Battery: 0 of 1,407,520 key streams pass (0 even at 5+ checks). Sentence key: best forced key letters score -4.931 (HOSSLACOLINTP|RACETORIPUS, not English) over 78.8M views. Join (207.6 billion alphabet pairs per key length and form, lengths 1-20): 1 fit in all, at key length 19 (9 checks, Beaufort form, plain SPAMD~keyed, cipher a K4-ciphertext order); its reading is gibberish, -7.15 on the big model over 60 quadgrams that include the clue words (English needs about -5.1), word cover 0.32; 0 fits whose key can be a dictionary word. Nothing at lengths 1-18 or 20.
controls: 3 shuffled K4s, full run each. Battery: 0, 0, 0. Sentence key: best -4.960, -4.829, -4.779 (two of three beat K4). Join: 47, 69 and 89 fits (all at lengths 16 and 18), best readings -6.76 each (gibberish), 0 word keys. Side check outside the logged run: 12 more shuffles gave 1-72 join fits; 3 of the 15 shuffles have 4 or fewer, so K4's single fit is inside the range.
planted: 5/5 exact (sliding key on the alphabet from K2's opening sentence; sliding key on Morse order; three-word messages with QWERTY as plain alphabet, with Morse order as cipher alphabet, and with new alphabets on both sides: each read back 97 of 97 letters, -4.23 to -4.59, key word named). Sentence-key score: 3/4 ranked first; the fourth ranked 7th (true key -5.006, noise top -4.681).
scope_limits: Only the listed orders: first-appearance orders from the K1, K2, K3 plaintexts (carved and corrected), K1-K3 joined, the K1-K4 ciphertext and the Morse text, from every starting letter, forwards and backwards, stopped after 1-26 different letters, unused letters appended in A-Z or Z-A order only; 7 typewriter orders, 6 Morse orders, 14 frequency orders. An arbitrary written chart stays open. Reversed forms only for the fixed orders and the read-to-the-end text orders (for the battery and the join a reversed alphabet is the same test with Vigenere and Beaufort swapped). Battery: one new alphabet against itself, A-Z or KRYPTOS; the rules and ranges of kryptos.round11.battery (repeating to 17, sliding to 15, progressive, autokey lags 1-6, two stacked keys to 13, chain addition), 7+ checks. Join: repeating key only, lengths 1-20, partner alphabet from the 666,994 dictionary alphabets or from the new list; lengths 21+ not tested; at lengths 16-20 fits exist by chance and the result rests on reading them. The sentence-key score is weak: it only sees a key whose 24 forced letters score above about -4.7, and it missed 1 of 4 planted keys; English keys only. The controls in the logged run are 3 shuffles. Overlap: idea 86 had already closed repeating and sliding keys for one unknown alphabet of any kind at most lengths.

negative.family: Non-keyword alphabets (text first-appearance orders, QWERTY, Morse, frequency)
negative.hypothesis: K4's tableau uses an alphabet mixed without a keyword: a keyphrase order taken from the sculpture's own texts, a typewriter order, a Morse-code order or a letter-frequency order, alone or paired with a dictionary keyword alphabet.
negative.scope: 140,752 alphabets (27 fixed orders, 9,047 read-to-the-end text orders, 122,574 phrase orders, 9,104 reversed) not in the dictionary set; round 11 key-rule battery on 5 layouts x Vigenere/Beaufort with 7+ checks (1.41M key streams); attack 57 sentence-key score (78.8M views); attack 63 hash join with a repeating key of length 1-20, new alphabet x 666,994 dictionary alphabets both ways round and new x new (8.3 trillion settings)
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: battery 0 passes; join 1 fit (length 19, reading -7.15, gibberish), none at lengths 1-18 or 20; sentence-key score no signal, K4 -4.931 (controls: 3 shuffled K4s give battery 0, join 47-89 fits with best -6.76, sentence key -4.960 to -4.779; planted 5/5 on the exact tests, 3/4 on the sentence-key score)

follow_ups: Run the other round 11 tests (68 clue alone / gap off by 1-3, 70 arithmetic mod 27-31, 71B fixed multipliers, 74 keyed-lag autokey) on the 140,752 non-keyword alphabets of kryptos.idea89_orders.new_alphabets, as idea 78 did for the transposition-mixed keyword alphabets.
